editorial.headline: Coconut Food Manufacturing With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 10793 covers coconut-based food products and is open nationally and in Bali for PMA registration under the record supplied.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 10793 is the manufacturing lane for coconut as food, not coconut as a vague plantation story.** The record defines it through the making of food products from coconut: thick and liquid coconut milk, powdered coconut milk, coconut sauce, sari kelapa in the form of nata de coco, dried grated coconut, coconut cream, and coconut flour. In plain English, this is where the coconut becomes a processed food ingredient or finished food product. The emphasis is on transformation: coconut is not merely handled, traded, or described as a raw commodity, but made into specific edible products that can sit inside a formal manufacturing activity.

That scope matters because it gives founders a clean commercial picture without needing to stretch the activity beyond the record. A business registering this activity could be built around one product line, such as coconut flour, or around a broader coconut-food processing operation that includes several of the named outputs. The record also makes the scale position unusually straightforward: the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the classification is not written only for industrial-scale operators. It can describe small, middle, and large manufacturing setups, as long as the actual activity remains within the coconut food products named in the scope.

The national foreign-ownership picture is equally direct. The record marks the PMA status as TERBUKA and gives a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. There is no partial cap to explain and no reduced percentage to soften. On the national reading supplied here, foreign investors may use this activity up to the full stated ceiling, with the source identified as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the clean national answer: this coconut food manufacturing activity is open for PMA, and the record’s maximum foreign ownership is 100%.

Bali does not change that answer in this record. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record says it is not blocked. The stated reason is: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The moratorium rule in the record blocks all Low plus Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across Bali, but this activity is not caught by that block on the supplied facts. So the honest national-vs-Bali reading is not a warning that Bali shuts the door. It is the opposite: nationally open, open at every listed business scale, and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the moratorium rule described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest reading is simple: KBLI 10793 is nationally open to full foreign ownership and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali on the supplied record.
